beats.beat: The company does not mine: it takes minerals and processes them into fine, chemically modified materials sold as specialty chemicals to industrial users.

Its product range splits into four buckets: Functional Additives and Chemically Modified Minerals — the two lines the filing calls its principal specialty-chemical business — plus Soft Minerals and Hard Minerals.

Sales run through the parent: a long-term arrangement gives 20 Microns Limited the job of marketing and selling the company's products over its network, which the filing calls a source of substantial synergies.
Customers do not sign long-term contracts. Sales are governed by purchase orders, so the volume, pricing and terms of every order are set individually; the filing lists this as a risk.
That makes customer concentration important: the top ten customers produced about 59% of revenue from operations in FY2015, 57% in FY2016 and 59% in FY2017.
Exports are a small second channel: the filing says exports of ₹1,068.18 lakh (₹10.68 crore) were achieved over the past five years, to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka.

The physical footprint is two manufacturing locations — GIDC Waghodia in Gujarat and Pathur Village, Tirunelveli in Tamil Nadu — plus administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur; the company does not own the premises of those plants and offices.
The filing's own strengths: a diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution, support of the holding company, continuous R&D and a strong management team.

beats.beat: The restated statements cover six periods: the six months to September 30, 2017, and the fiscal years ended March 31, 2017, 2016, 2015, 2014 and 2013. Amounts below are converted from ₹ lakh to ₹ crore.
Profit after tax: -₹0.27 crore in FY2013 and -₹0.12 crore in FY2014, then ₹1.50 crore in FY2015, ₹0.90 crore in FY2016, ₹1.75 crore in FY2017 and ₹1.33 crore in H1 FY2018.

Operating cash flow: ₹2.01 crore in FY2013, ₹1.28 crore in FY2014, ₹4.22 crore in FY2015, ₹8.03 crore in FY2016, -₹3.50 crore in FY2017 and ₹1.25 crore in H1 FY2018. The FY2017 outflow happened in a year the company still reported a profit.
Total assets: ₹30.19 crore at FY2013-end, ₹26.79 crore at FY2014-end, ₹25.93 crore at FY2015-end, ₹27.67 crore at FY2016-end, ₹32.74 crore at FY2017-end and ₹34.25 crore at September 30, 2017.
Basic earnings per share: ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.43 in FY2017 and ₹1.48 in H1 FY2018, after negative EPS in FY2013 and FY2014.
Revenue from operations, EBITDA and debt levels are not in the extracted portions of the restated statements, so the top line and leverage trend cannot be shown from this digest.

beats.beat: Four promoters: three individuals — Chandresh S. Parikh, Atil C. Parikh and Rajesh C. Parikh — plus corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited.
Pre-issue, the promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares — 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity capital. The rest, 21,510 shares (0.24%), sits with other entities in the promoter group.
As at September 30, 2017, authorised share capital is ₹2,000 lakh and issued, subscribed and paid-up capital is ₹897 lakh.
Related-party transactions have occurred over the last five financial years and the six months to September 30, 2017, and the filing says the company may continue them.

Other governance flags: the company does not own the premises of its main plants and offices, it has not yet obtained certain licences and approvals for the factory at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, and there have been past instances of non-filing, wrong filing or delays with the RoC.

beats.beat: The company sits in India's specialty chemicals industry. The DRHP says the segment holds roughly 17% of the Indian chemicals industry, about ₹1,000 billion, and separately cites a ₹1,443 billion market figure.
Growth is double-digit: the specialty chemicals segment grew at 10-12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017, and CRISIL Research forecasts 12-14% CAGR going forward.

The filing's fastest niches: construction chemicals, water chemicals and personal-care ingredients each expected to grow at 15% CAGR; surfactants at 13%; textile chemicals and flavours & fragrances at 12%; polymer additives at 10%; polymer demand at 9-10% and plastic products at 11-13%.
Competition is fragmented: SMEs hold 70-75% of the market, and only a few Indian players have the scale to take on global giants on product development and innovation.

Demand drivers are macro: GDP grew 7.1% in FY2017, private consumption accounts for 58% of GDP, urbanisation is rising, the DRHP sees the middle class reaching 148 million households by 2030, and the government has drafted a National Chemical Policy while allowing 100% FDI in the sector.

Import substitution is the company's stated hook: chemicals imports grew at 6.4% CAGR against exports at 6% CAGR, and China's stricter environmental rules since 2015 have reduced its chemical manufacturing output.

The headwinds the filing acknowledges: imports consistently exceeding exports, a fragmented market that invites pricing pressure, strict EU regulation under REACH for exporters, and changing tax and regulatory laws.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes minerals and chemicals into specialty materials — functional additives, chemically modified minerals, soft minerals and hard minerals — for industrial buyers, and sells them mainly through the network of its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited.
It is raising money through an SME public issue to fund a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and to list on NSE EMERGE, the SME platform of NSE.

This is a small company: total assets were ₹34.25 crore at September 30, 2017, its best full-year profit in the disclosed period was ₹1.75 crore in FY2017, and before the issue its promoters held 99.76% of the equity.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, why it is raising money, and how small the business is in absolute terms.

beats.beat: The issue is managed by Vivro Financial Services Private Limited, with Link Intime India Private Limited as registrar.

The money raised is earmarked for three stated objects: capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; general corporate purposes; and creating a public trading market by listing on NSE EMERGE to enhance visibility and brand.

The available excerpts do not state the total issue size, the fresh-issue versus offer-for-sale split, the price band, or the identity of any selling shareholder. This report will describe those as not disclosed rather than estimate them.

beats.beat: Customer concentration without contracts: the top ten customers bring roughly 59% of revenue, and sales are on purchase orders with no long-term agreements — one lost customer or renegotiated price hits revenue immediately.
Negative cash flow in a profitable year: FY2017 net profit was ₹1.75 crore but operating cash flow was -₹3.50 crore; the DRHP itself calls out negative cash flows in previous years as a risk factor.

Regulatory gaps: certain statutory licences, registrations and approvals needed to operate the factory at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia are not yet obtained, and there have been past RoC filing lapses — so penalties remain possible.

Dependence on the parent's sales network: marketing and sales rely on a long-term arrangement with 20 Microns Limited, so any disruption to that network or relationship would expose the company's revenue directly.
Legal and contingent liabilities: the company, its promoters, group company and directors are parties to legal proceedings, and contingent liabilities aggregate ₹29.11 lakh as at September 30, 2017.
